# Run a task in a sandbox

## 1. Set up the sandbox
- Confirm you're in a git repository (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`). If not, say sandboxing needs git and stop.
- Make a short kebab-case slug from the task description.
- Create an isolated worktree on a new branch, as a sibling directory: `git worktree add ../<repo-name>.sandbox-<slug> -b sandbox/<slug>` (from the current branch, or the base branch the user named). If that path already exists, add a short suffix.
- If the task needs real OS-level isolation (untrusted code, unfamiliar dependencies) and Docker is available (`docker info` succeeds), you may additionally run the work inside a container that mounts the worktree — pick an image for the detected stack (Python: `python:3.12`, Node: `node:lts`, Go: `golang:1`, Rust: `rust:1`, otherwise a generic Debian/Ubuntu image) and have the subagent issue its commands through `docker exec`. Otherwise just use the worktree directly — don't block on Docker.

## 2. Delegate the task
- Delegate this to the `coding-plugin:sandbox-worker` subagent. If subagents are unavailable, follow `references/sandbox-worker.md` yourself.
- Give the subagent: the absolute sandbox path, the branch name, and the task description verbatim. Tell it explicitly: all work stays under that path; never touch the original working tree.

## 3. Report, don't merge
- Show the subagent's summary, plus `git -C <sandbox path> diff --stat <base>`.
- Give the user the exact commands to review (`cd <path> && git diff <base>`), merge (`git merge sandbox/<slug>`), or discard (`git worktree remove <path> && git branch -D sandbox/<slug>`).
- Do not merge, push, open a pull/merge request, or remove the worktree yourself — leave the result in place for the user to inspect.

## Limitations
- This is directory/branch isolation for review purposes, not a security sandbox: the subagent runs with the same OS user and permissions as the rest of the session. Only an actual container (step 1) adds a real process/filesystem boundary, and even then only to the extent that container restricts the mount.
- The project's git hooks (`.githooks/pre-commit`, `pre-push`) still run inside the sandbox worktree, since `core.hooksPath` is a repository-wide git setting shared by every worktree — so secret scanning and protected-path/branch checks still apply when the subagent commits or pushes from the sandbox. Whether your agent's own live-session guards (e.g. Claude Code's PreToolUse/Stop hooks) also cover the subagent's work inside the sandbox depends on how your agent runs subagents — don't rely on them there. Rely on the git-hook and CI layers, plus your own review of the diff, before merging.
